title: Monitoring Hierarchies in Knowledge Production
abstract: arXiv:2609.10499v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study peer monitoring design in knowledge production. A principal leads agents who work on different but related tasks. By working on their own tasks, agents acquire information that is useful for evaluating their peers' performance. We consider robust contracts under which effort by all agents is the unique rationalizable outcome. The optimal contract induces a hierarchy of monitoring authority: agents easier for the principal to monitor directly are assigned greater authority to evaluate other agents. Task diversity improves information value but weakens peer monitoring. This tension distorts optimal public task assignment toward the principal's core expertise. Confidential random assignment relaxes this distortion by decoupling information production from the perceived monitoring structure.

translated_title: 知识生产中的监督层级
translated_abstract: 我们研究知识生产中的同伴监督设计问题。一个委托人领导着从事不同但相关任务的多个代理人。代理人通过完成自己的任务，会获得有助于评估其同伴绩效的信息。我们考虑稳健合同，即在该合同下所有代理人的努力是唯一可理性化的结果。最优合同会诱导出一个监督权威的层级结构：对委托人而言更容易直接监督的代理人，会被赋予更大的评估其他代理人的权力。任务多样性提升了信息价值，但削弱了同伴监督。这种张力使最优的公开任务分配被扭曲地偏向委托人的核心专长领域。而保密的随机任务分配通过将信息生产与被感知的监督结构解耦，缓解了这一扭曲。
tldr: 该论文证明最优稳健合同会在知识生产中形成监督权威层级——越容易被委托人直接监督的代理人获得越大的评估同伴的权力，而保密随机任务分配可缓解任务多样性带来的信息价值与同伴监督之间的内在张力。
en_tdlr: The optimal robust contract induces a monitoring hierarchy in knowledge production—agents easier for the principal to monitor directly are granted greater authority to evaluate their peers—and confidential random task assignment mitigates the tension between information value and peer monitoring arising from task diversity.
